front: Where is the safety catch on the T3x Arctic?
back: Right side, just behind the bolt handle (95%, Tikka manual page 8).

front: Tikka safety: what does the red dot mean?
back: Safety OFF: the rifle can fire (95%, page 8).

front: Tikka safety ON locks which 3 things?
back: The bolt closed, the firing pin cocked, the sear and trigger (95%, page 8).

front: Can the Tikka safety go ON when the rifle is uncocked?
back: No. It only engages when cocked. Unloaded, uncocked, safety forward is the transport position (95%).

front: How do you take the bolt out?
back: Lift the handle, press the bolt stop on the left side, pull the bolt fully back (95%, pages 8 and 13).

front: The 4 bolt moves?
back: Up (unlock, cock), back (case out), forward (feed), down (lock) (95%).

front: Load check, step 1?
back: Muzzle safe, finger off, safety forward: red dot showing (95%, page 8).

front: Load check: after the chamber is checked empty?
back: Bolt in and closed: it is cocked. Muzzle safe, press the trigger to decock (95%, page 8).

front: Unloading order on the Tikka?
back: Safety forward, lift and pull back to extract the round, magazine out, check, close, decock (95%, page 10).

front: Why keep the bolt back until the magazine is out?
back: Pushing it forward with the magazine in feeds the next round (Tip).

front: Loading the magazine?
back: Round on the follower in front of the lips, press down, slide back under the lips. Never force extra (95%, page 10).

front: Emptying the magazine?
back: Thumb pushes the rim forward, index finger tips the round up and out (95%, pages 10 and 11).

front: Click, no bang?
back: Muzzle safe, wait at least 1 minute, unload with extreme care (95%, pages 10 and 19).

front: Hand the rifle over only when?
back: Magazine out, bolt open, chamber visually checked (95%, page 8).

front: Your 10 round Tikka magazine and the 5 round limit?
back: The limit is for magazines designed for semi automatic firearms. A bolt action magazine is not on that list (90%, my reading of SOR/98-462).

front: Factory barrel length of the T3x Arctic?
back: 508 mm (20 in), 1 turn in 10 in twist (95%, Sako).

front: How does the law measure barrel length?
back: Muzzle to and including the chamber, without muzzle devices (99%, Criminal Code s. 84(2)).

front: Altered rifle: prohibited below what lengths?
back: Under 660 mm overall, or a barrel under 457 mm (99%, s. 84(1)). Never cut it.

front: Arctic front sight: clockwise on the elevation screw does?
back: Post goes down, shots go up. About 7 mm per click at 100 m (95%, page 11).

front: Arctic windage: how?
back: Loosen the rear screw on the side you want the drum to move to, snug the other side (95%, page 12).

front: Iron sight click math at 100 m?
back: Clicks = cm off / 0.7 (95%).

front: What must you never open on the rear drum?
back: The screw in the drum centre: spring parts fly out (95%, page 12).

front: Rear sight set screw torque? Front sight screw?
back: 0.8 Nm (7 in lb). 5 Nm (44 in lb) (95%, page 11).

front: How far is the bore sight target in the manual?
back: About 25 to 30 m, bolt out. Final sighting in at 100 to 150 m (95%, page 12).

front: Why is a scope tricky on the Arctic?
back: The rear drum sits behind a short Picatinny rail, under where the scope passes. High rings, or drum off (75 to 95%).

front: Receiver screw torque, metal trigger guard?
back: 7 Nm (62 in lb). Plastic guard: max 5 Nm (95%, page 13).

front: Leupold BackCountry cross slot ring torque?
back: Ring top screws 28 in lb, keeper clamp 45 in lb (95%, Leupold).

front: Where do ring torque numbers come from?
back: Only the ring maker's sheet. Tikka gives none (95%).

front: Eye relief on a .308?
back: About 9 cm (3.5 in) or more. Set it on top power (65 to 85%).

front: 1/4 MOA (minute of angle) scope click at 100 m?
back: About 0.73 cm (70%).

front: Dry fire with a snap cap or a dummy round?
back: Snap cap. Dummies do not protect the firing pin (95%, page 9).

front: What does the plate test give you?
back: Your range from each position: the last distance with 5 of 5 in a paper plate (Tip).

front: Can a bipod go on the Tikka?
back: Yes, on the front sling stud (95%, page 16).

front: Which bullet is unlawful for hunting in BC?
back: Full metal jacketed non expanding, tracer, incendiary or explosive (99%, synopsis).

front: Tikka's ammunition rules?
back: Factory CIP or SAAMI, inspect each round, nothing over 10 years, never steel jacketed bullets (95%, page 9).

front: Black tailed buck weight?
back: About 48 to 90 kg (90%, BC deer account).

front: Cleaning rod direction?
back: Breech to muzzle through a rod guide, bullet direction only (95%, page 18).

front: Before the first shot after cleaning?
back: Wipe the chamber dry (95%, page 18).

front: The 3 grease points?
back: Locking lugs, cocking cam, cocking piece head (95%, page 7).

front: Bolt strip: when does the screwdriver come out of the gap?
back: Only when you are ready to refit the shroud (95%, page 13).

front: Bolt shroud off a right handed T3x bolt?
back: Turn it clockwise until it stops, pull it away (95%, page 13).

front: Lowest Tikka trigger weight allowed?
back: 11 N (2.5 lb). Factory 13 to 15 N (95%, page 15).

front: Rust can start how soon if not cleaned?
back: Within 24 hours, even on stainless (95%, page 18).

front: Wet rifle tonight?
back: Out of the case, dry in warm, dry air, then the routine clean. No leather or fabric case for storage (95%, pages 18 and 19).

front: Muzzle went into snow?
back: Unload, bolt out, look through. Any obstruction: gunsmith (95%, page 9).

front: Is a suppressor legal in Canada?
back: No. A device to muffle a firearm is a prohibited device (99%, s. 84(1)).

front: More than 2 length of pull spacers need?
back: Longer recoil pad screws. Do not overtighten (95%, page 15).

front: Range day: what is the cold bore bull?
back: Your first shot from a cold, clean barrel next time: like a hunting shot (Tip).
